findings.text: The first paragraph says plainly what Athena is and how it differs from other tools, so a newcomer can say what it is within seconds.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: A next-step link near the top lets a newcomer skip the long study and go straight to install, which works well.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The page at Athena's home address is titled for a different project, firstmate, which a newcomer has probably never heard of. Most of the page describes firstmate's internals, and Athena gets about three sentences.
findings.source:
/

Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: The install steps do not say how to get a checkout, what is needed first (Rust toolchain, AI model access or API keys), or that `athena ask` has to run inside a git repository. A newcomer would need to go to the GitHub repo to actually start.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The page names these selling points but never shows them: there is no sample of a run, a check, or a cost record. The only evidence of what Athena produces is the study itself.
findings.source: lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: Even the 'Start here' section quickly fills with exit codes and terms that are never defined. 'Unheld', 'merge authority', 'wake', 'heartbeat', 'endpoint' and 'durable record' have no glossary entries.
findings.source: Start here > One piece of work: "A spawn is accepted only for an unheld, unblocked item." and "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75"

findings.text: This glossary entry does not say what a ship is. The plainer definition is earlier on the page: "A ship changes a project".
findings.source: Glossary, ship: "A kind of task, named next to scouts."

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This makes the page a convincing demonstration of the traceability that Athena advertises.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: The page says openly what the study did not do, such as running firstmate, which helps a reader trust it.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: This note does not say which repository holds the `studies/` folder, so a newcomer cannot find it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
